SIXTH CHORDS AND SIX/NINE CHORDS

Sixth chords are major or minor chords with an added major 6th degree (1-3-5-6 or 1->3~5-6). (A common mistake is to add a minor 6th to a minor sixth chord.) They have a jazzy sound and work great in jazz and blues (. Fig. 7 eighth-position chords omit the 5th degree. Omitting the 5th is common practice with guitar voicings. In most cases, this does- n't have any impact on the naming of the chord.

Fig. 7

Six/nine chords are major or minor chords with an added 6th and 9th (1-3-5-6-9 and 1+3-5-6-9). Quite common in Latin, they have a pretty sound and work great for ending chords (Fig. 8).

Fig. 8
